    Tech Report: cPanel to Microsoft 365 Migration: Step-by-Step, MX Cutover Included

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, to migrate a cPanel domain to Microsoft 365, you create licensed mailboxes, copy each cPanel mailbox with an IMAP migration batch, and then point the domain's MX record at Microsoft 365.
    • It has been revealed that updated 22 Nov 2026: the split-delivery steps were corrected after a hands-on test.
    • Industry observers note that this guide is for administrators of a small or mid-sized organization whose email lives on cPanel hosting and who are moving to Exchange Online.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, to migrate a cPanel domain to Microsoft 365, you create licensed mailboxes, copy each cPanel mailbox with an IMAP migration batch, and then point the domain's MX record at Microsoft 365. If everyone cannot move on the same day, you set up split delivery first so that mail for the domain reaches whichever system holds the mailbox. Only mail moves; contacts, calendars and tasks do not, and the MX record stays untouched until the last step is tested.

    It has been revealed that updated 22 Nov 2026: the split-delivery steps were corrected after a hands-on test. The first version used a mail flow rule ("recipient is Outside the organization" and recipient domain is the shared domain) with a rule-scoped Partner connector; on a live tenant that rule never matched, and mail to cPanel-only addresses bounced with 554 5.4.14 Hop count exceeded - possible mail loop. The guide now uses an On-premises connector used only when email is sent to the domain, which delivered to the cPanel server in the same test. If you built the earlier version, see "Convert a rule-based setup" below.

    Industry observers note that this guide is for administrators of a small or mid-sized organization whose email lives on cPanel hosting and who are moving to Exchange Online. It covers one domain, either moved in a single weekend or in phases. By the end you will have:.

    It has been revealed that the generic mechanics of an IMAP batch (CSV columns, endpoint options, throttling) are in the IMAP to Exchange Online migration guide; this article does not repeat them line by line. It adds the cPanel-specific plan, the phased route, the cutover order and the cleanup. The email migration cutover checklist is a good companion for the DNS day.

    Placeholders used throughout: example.com is your domain, admin@example.com is the Microsoft 365 admin, yourtenant.onmicrosoft.com is the tenant's default domain, mail.example.com is the cPanel mail host, and 203.0.113.10 is the IP address the cPanel server sends mail from (on shared hosting this can differ from the address of mail.example.com).

    Recent findings suggest that if you can do one cutover, do it: it has fewer moving parts. The phased route in the section "Phased moves with split delivery" is the same migration plus a routing layer.

    Before touching Microsoft 365, write down what exists on the cPanel side.

    In a recent development, leave the MX record pointing at cPanel. Do not add the Microsoft 365 MX, SPF or autodiscover records yet.

    In a recent development, in cPanel, open the mail client settings for any mailbox (under Email > Email Accounts). Use the incoming server name shown for the secure SSL/TLS settings and IMAP port 993. The migration endpoint in the next step needs exactly that name, for example mail.example.com.

    The CSV needs EmailAddress, UserName and Password. Attributes cannot contain spaces. You have three ways to get working credentials:.

    The CSV is a list of working passwords. Store it somewhere restricted and delete it, and the temporary cPanel passwords, when the migration is done. If the file has non-ASCII characters, save it as UTF-8.

    In a recent development, connect to Exchange Online PowerShell, test the source, then create the endpoint and batch. Use a small test batch of two or three mailboxes first.

    Recent findings suggest that the same steps exist in the Exchange admin center under Migration: Endpoints > Add > IMAP, then Add migration batch > Migrate to Exchange Online > IMAP migration, selecting your endpoint and importing the CSV on Add user mailboxes. Check the real folder names in a mail client before you exclude any, because they differ between hosts.

    Sources indicate that microsoft's migration user status documentation describes these states: Queued (batch running, user not started, typically because all endpoint connections are busy), Synced (initial sync done; for IMAP it can also mean an incremental sync succeeded), Failed (provisioning or the initial sync failed), and Completed. In the Exchange admin center, select the batch under Migration and use View details in the details pane for the per-user report, where Stop migration and Resume migration appear depending on the user's status.

    According to recent reports, the per-user report is a plain list of events. Microsoft does not document each line, so treat this as practical interpretation, not a specification:.

    Worry about a Failed status with an Error text (usually a wrong or changed password, or a blocked connection), repeated connection errors in the report (network or the host's connection limits), and a non-zero SkippedItemCount (items over 35 MB or beyond the item limit). Add -IncludeSkippedItems to see which items were skipped. The stuck migration batch article covers slow batches.

    In a recent development, split delivery lets one domain live on two systems. Mail enters through Microsoft 365 (the MX record points there), and a recipient that exists in Exchange Online is delivered there; any other recipient in that domain is relayed to cPanel. Microsoft's mail flow guidance recommends pointing MX at Microsoft 365 for the most accurate spam filtering when mailboxes are in two places.

    The three steps, in the order to do them:.

    Do all three and test before you change MX. The Microsoft 365 split delivery guide covers other second hosts (Google Workspace, Zoho), the reverse direction and a longer troubleshooting table.

    Recent findings suggest that microsoft defines Authoritative as delivering to listed recipients and rejecting unknown ones. Internal relay delivers to known recipients in Microsoft 365 and relays unknown ones to your own server, and requires a connector to that server. In the Exchange admin center go to Mail flow > Accepted domains, select example.com, and under This accepted domain is choose Internal relay, then Save. In PowerShell:.

    Industry observers note that in Mail flow > Connectors, select + Add a connector and set Connection from to Office 365 and Connection to to Your organization's email server. That makes an On-premises connector, which Microsoft describes as one that "services domains that are used by your on-premises organization"; Partner organization is for domains external to your organization, which example.com is not. Then:.

    Recent findings suggest that -RecipientDomains example.com makes the connector apply only to mail for your domain, -UseMXRecord $false sends it to the smart host instead of following MX (which would point back to Microsoft 365 after the cutover), and -IsTransportRuleScoped $false means no rule is involved. -TlsSettings EncryptionOnly encrypts the channel without certificate authentication; CertificateValidation and DomainValidation (with -TlsDomain) are stricter and are better if the cPanel server has a valid certificate for its name.

    Why this works: a recipient with a mailbox, or any other recipient object, in Microsoft 365 is delivered inside the tenant and never reaches the connector. Only a recipient that Microsoft 365 cannot resolve goes out, and because the address is in example.com, it matches the connector's recipient domain. Microsoft's connector page notes the service first picks "a connector that exactly matches the recipient domain.".

    If you already built the rule version (a rule-scoped connector plus a rule that redirects to it), delete the rule first, then change the connector:.

    Two things came up in the hands-on test. Changing the connector's scope while a rule still referenced it, even a disabled rule, failed with Error executing request. One or more transport rules are still referencing the specified connector.; deleting the rule fixed it. And the Exchange admin center did not offer a way to change an existing connector from Partner organization to Your organization's email server, so use Set-OutboundConnector -ConnectorType OnPremises or create a new connector.

    Sources indicate that A rule with The recipient is located > Outside the organization plus recipient domain is example.com looks like the obvious way to catch cPanel people, but Microsoft's definitions rule it out. The mail flow rule conditions page notes a recipient is inside the organization if "The recipient's email address is in an accepted domain that's configured as an authoritative domain or in an internal relay domain, and the message was sent or received over an authenticated connection", and outside only if the address "isn't in an accepted domain" or is in an external relay domain. An Internal relay domain is an accepted domain, so the rule never matches. In the hands-on test the mail then followed the MX record, which pointed back at Microsoft 365, and bounced with 554 5.4.14 Hop count exceeded - possible mail loop; every hop in the bounce was an outlook.com server and nothing reached cPanel, even after 30 minutes. The domain-scoped connector avoids the problem because it matches on the recipient domain.

    Send from a Microsoft 365 user to a cPanel-only user: it must arrive in cPanel webmail, and the message trace (see Message trace in Exchange Online) must show it leaving through the To cPanel connector. Check the trace, not just arrival: while MX still points at cPanel, mail can arrive by ordinary MX routing even when no connector matched. Then send from cPanel to a moved user and confirm it arrives in Microsoft 365 through the forwarder. The Exchange Online connectors guide explains the connector objects used here.

    Do this once the batch has synced and, if phased, the test above passed.

    On shared hosting, the IP address the server sends mail from can differ from the address mail.example.com resolves to, so do not copy the IP from DNS. In cPanel open Email > Email Deliverability, click Manage for the domain, and read the IP in the Suggested "SPF" (TXT) Record; cPanel states it automatically includes the server's main IPv4 or IPv6 addresses there. If that address is 203.0.113.10, the record is:.

    ip4: authorizes the cPanel server, the include authorizes Microsoft 365, and ~all soft-fails everything else. Microsoft allows only one SPF record per domain and notes multiple records cause permerror, so edit the existing record instead of adding a second one (cPanel may already have published one). Receivers also stop at 10 DNS lookups: counted the way Microsoft documents it, ip4: and all cost nothing, each include: costs one plus whatever is nested inside it, and a or mx cost one each. This record uses one direct lookup. Once nothing else sends mail, tighten to v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all, Microsoft's recommended form.

    It has been revealed that after the MX change, send from an outside account such as Gmail to a moved user and to a cPanel-only user. Both must arrive, the message trace should show the cPanel message leaving through the To cPanel connector, and the outside sender should not get a BoxTrapper challenge. The SPF, DKIM and DMARC setup guide covers the policy side.

    During coexistence both systems send mail as your domain, so both need to authenticate. For Microsoft 365, publish the two CNAME records Microsoft documents, with hostnames selector1._domainkey and selector2._domainkey, pointing to the values from your tenant:.

    If the cPanel server already signs mail, its key sits under its own selector name, so check the existing DNS TXT records before you add records. Start DMARC at a monitoring policy and review reports before you tighten it, as Microsoft advises for complex mail sources.

    Recent findings suggest that for clients, latest Outlook profiles use autodiscover. Remove old IMAP accounts from phones and Outlook, add the Microsoft 365 account, and let it download mail. Consumers also need their contacts and calendars moved by hand, since the IMAP migration does not carry them.

    What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you want to pay online, you need to register an account and provide credit card information.
    • Sources indicate that imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information.
    • In a recent development, it’s like your computer’s hard drive.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you want to pay online, you need to register an account and provide credit card information. If you don't have a credit card, you can pay with bank transfer. With the rise of cryptocurrencies, these methods may become old.Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain. Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.So, What is Blockchain?A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, on 22 November 2026 NVIDIA released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a compact ~2B-parameter reasoning vision-language-action model that intends driving trajectories and can emit Chain-of-Causation explanations. It targets DRIVE AGX Thor, not a datacenter card. With the FP8 + TensorRT Edge-LLM recipe (DRIVE OS 7.2.7.0, CUDA 13.4, TensorRT 11.3.1.9) NVIDIA measures 160–190 ms pixel-to-trajectory latency, depending on how much reasoning is generated. Adaptive reasoning skips full traces during routine driving and emits NOMINAL tokens instead. The BF16 PyTorch path needs 16 GB+ and is slower (demo numbers revealed ~0.76 Hz); the optimized path is what makes the real-time claim.

    It has been revealed that that latency number is the interesting part for anyone shipping live overlays on Windows. 160–190 ms from sensor to action is the same ballpark as a usable first partial from a streaming STT session once the audio has left the capture callback. The model side keeps improving. The capture side on Windows has not.

    A dual-track overlay for interviews or calls needs two clean PCM streams that stay separate:.

    Industry observers note that audio-thread callbacks do nothing but copy samples into a lock-free SPSC ring (power-of-two capacity). No model work, no locks that can stall the callback. Consumer threads then resample to 16 kHz mono, run a cheap energy/VAD gate, and feed either a local streaming session or chunked local model.

    Typical additive budget once samples leave the callback (measured on a mid-range Windows 11 laptop, shared mode with enhancements off):.

    Industry observers note that alpamayo’s 160–190 ms is the model-plus-optimization stage on specialized silicon. On a laptop the equivalent stage is your local ASR or small suggestion model. If the capture period is a 40 ms Bluetooth shared-mode buffer plus engine APOs, the recognizer starts late regardless of how good the model is.

    Once the two tracks are clean and separated you can:.

    Sources indicate that drop audio engine enhancements, pin the capture thread, request the shortest period the engine will honor, and keep the ring lock-free. Those changes reclaim the largest slice of the budget. The rest is model selection and paint time.

    Industry observers note that NVIDIA’s adaptive-reasoning trick (skip tokens when the scene is routine) has an analogue here: skip the suggestion model when energy is low or the transcript is unchanged. The capture path still has to be correct first.

    如何遍历 比如是tx数据，我们发现不是直接获取的实体数据，为什么这样呢？如果你要获取某个范围的tx数据，或者找寻某一个特定tx。 如果采用实体数据的话，这其中按设计来说，会有一个传递，你怎么传送这个巨大的数据呢？ 然后给另一个函数处理。 当然硬要传送，也强行能实现，就是需要申请巨大的内存。 或者我直接一边读取一边处理，这样可能不利于模块化设计。 我们来看btc源码是怎么处理的，以部分tx为例。 是为每一个tx建立索引，在bool LoadWallet()中，把钱包相关的索引读取出来。 放在mapWallet中，这样就不需要很多内存，就可以实时保存这份数据表。 供后续很方便的查找。 如何保存索引 我们可以看到，索引加载到内存后，并不是vector这样的形式存在于内存中。 而是一个哈希值对应一个索引。 map mapWallet; 像这样的，像当于给每个索引定义了一个编号id吧。 这样查找时候也很方便。 这样，先找索引，再根据索引去读数据，我们就不必每次读取大量的实体数据，然后操作这份实体数据，然后才决定是否使用某个实体数据。而是先根据索引得到结果。再读取数据。.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Originally published on Medium: https://medium.com/@supsabhi/kotlin-scope-functions-finally-explained-without-the-confusion-0cb943d6ced2?sharedUserId=supsabhi.

    Master these once, and suddenly every Kotlin codebase starts making a lot more sense.

    If you’ve been learning Kotlin, chances are you’ve come across scope functions and thought:.

    “Why are there FIVE of them… and why do they all look the same?” 😅.

    It has been revealed that when I first encountered Kotlin’s scope functions, my reaction was something similar.So don’t worry, you’re not alone.Scope functions are one of those Kotlin features that looks confusing on the surface but becomes genuinely delightful once it clicks. This article is that click..!

    In this article, I’ll break down **SCOPE FUNCTIONS **in the simplest way possible — no jargon, just intuition and examples.By the end, you’ll know exactly what each one does, when to reach for it, and — just as importantly — when not to.

    So, what even is a scope function?

    A scope function is a function that executes a block of code within the context of an object. That’s the official definition, and it’s honestly not very helpful on its own.Let me try again.

    Imagine you’re setting up a newly introduced User object. Without scope functions, you’d do this:.

    According to recent reports, that works fine. But notice how you keep writing user. over and over?

    Scope functions let you “enter” the object for a moment, do everything you need, and step back out — without repeating yourself:.

    Cleaner, right? That’s the essence of it.

    Basically all scope functions do the same thing:.

    👉 They run a block of code using an object.

    🔍 Let’s Understand Them One by One.

    1.let — Safe Calls & Transformations. — Use it · Returns the lambda result.

    let takes the object as it inside the block, and returns whatever the last expression in the block evaluates to.

    👉 Here, it represents the object (name).

    2.run — Initialize + Compute Result — Use this · Returns the lambda result.

    run is like let, but instead of it, the object becomes this inside the block — so you can access its members directly without a prefix.

    3. with — Operate on an Object (Non-extension)-Use this · Returns the lambda result · Not an extension.

    with is the odd one out — you pass the object as an argument rather than calling it on the object. Everything else is similar to run.

    👉 Cleaner than repeating person.name, person.age.

    It has been revealed that 4. apply — Object Configuration — Use this · Returns the object itself.

    Sources indicate that this is the builder’s best friend. apply gives you this inside the block, and when you’re done, it returns the original object — not the result of the block.

    val person = Person().apply { name = "John" age = 25 } This is perfect for configuring an object right after creating it. The classic use case for object initialization.

    5.also — Side Effects (Logging, Debugging) — Use it · Returns the object itself.

    In a recent development, also is like apply, but uses it instead of this. It’s great when you want to do something extra with the object — like log it — without interrupting the main flow.

    👉 It returns the original object unchanged.

    Instead of memorizing everything, just remember this:.

    A real-world example that uses all five.

    According to recent reports, here’s a contrived-but-illustrative snippet that indicates them all working together. Don’t use all five in one chain like this in real code — but it’s a great way to see the differences side by side.

    Because each one solves a slightly different problem:.

    In a recent development, using apply when you need a result. If you find yourself ending an apply block with a value you want to capture, switch to run. apply always gives you back the object, ignoring your last expression.

    According to recent reports, chaining scope functions for no reason. Scope functions make code more readable — but only when used purposefully. If a plain if statement is clearer, use it. Readability wins.

    Sources indicate that forgetting that with isn’t null-safe. You can’t do nullableObj?.with { … } because with isn’t an extension function. Reach for let or run when null safety is involved.

    Scope functions are one of those things you pick up gradually. At first, scope functions feel like overkill. But once you start using them:.

    It has been revealed that don’t try to memorize them — instead, start using just let and apply, which cover 80% of cases. The others will start feeling natural as you read more Kotlin code. The next time you see let, run, or apply… don’t panic — you’re just one scope away from cleaner Kotlin 😄.. Happy Scoping..!!

    Tech Report: PHP 8.3.37 Fixed 5 Critical Bugs on 19 November. Which Ones Reach a Laravel App?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1647 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • On 19 November PHP shipped 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36, alongside the first stable 8.6.0.
    • It has been revealed that I patched it.
    • In a recent development, the answer surprised me a little.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Originally published at hafiz.dev.

    On 19 November PHP shipped 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36, alongside the first stable 8.6.0. The 8.3.37 changelog lists 13 security fixes. Five of them are rated critical, every one at 9.2 on CVSS v4. My production server, a single Ubuntu box with several sites behind nginx and PHP-FPM, was still on 8.3.36 the next morning.

    It has been revealed that I patched it. But first I read every critical advisory and asked one question of each. What would an attacker need from a Laravel app for this to work?

    In a recent development, the answer surprised me a little. Most of them need something a stock Laravel app never does. And the ones that could still matter depend on what else shares the server, not on Laravel. One setting even changed during the upgrade, although nobody touched php.ini.

    The release announcement is short. It says this is a security release and encourages all 8.3 customers to upgrade. The detail lives in the changelog and the php-src security advisories. Three of the five critical fixes are in ext-session, PHP's own session extension. One is in ext-date and one is in PHP-FPM.

    In a recent development, so for each fix, the question becomes concrete. Does the bug need PHP's native session machinery, a specific php.ini, or a specific web server setup?

    In a recent development, the other eight fixes in the 8.3 branch cover SOAP, Phar signatures, the FPM status page, PHP-CGI and the HTTP stream wrappers. Four of them are rated high. Worth patching, but none of them is the reason to patch today.

    It has been revealed that the serializer mismatch is the one with the scariest headline, so I started there. PHP's session upload progress feature tracks a running upload by writing progress data into the visitor's session. The PHP manual says plainly when that happens. "The upload progress information is written to the session before any scripts are executed.".

    Recent findings suggest that that's only half the attack, though. The advisory needs a second step, something that reads the same stored session with a different serializer and then deserializes it with a gadget chain available. In a Laravel app nothing reads /var/lib/php/sessions. Laravel's file driver writes to storage/framework/sessions through its own handler.

    Recent findings suggest that so what reads native sessions on a typical Laravel server? Usually nothing. On my box the native session directory was empty:.

    But a server that also hosts a WordPress site, an old admin panel or a phpMyAdmin install is a different story. Those use native sessions. The partially overwritten session files bug needs the same thing, native file sessions with attacker influence over the data.

    Sources indicate that the interrupted shutdown use-after-free is the subtle one. It's an incomplete fix for one of October's advisories (CVE-2026-109619), and it claims outright that disabling upload progress does nothing for it. It needs a native session whose cleanup hits a fatal error. Then the next request on the same FPM worker touches freed memory, and that request doesn't need to belong to the same user or the same site. My server runs every site in one FPM pool called www. So if any of those sites used native sessions, a Laravel site sharing the worker would inherit the problem. The advisory says it could lead to code execution, although that hasn't been demonstrated yet. But "shared worker" is exactly the kind of detail I'd rather not argue about.

    Sources indicate that PHP reads php://input lazily. If a code path opens the stream and stops early (the advisory's example is a malformed multipart body that makes PHP's parser stop at a predictable position), the rest of the body stays unread on the connection.

    In a recent development, on a normal nginx setup that's harmless. nginx closes the FastCGI connection after each request, and the leftover bytes go with it. With persistent connections they don't. The leftover bytes get parsed as the next FastCGI request, and an attacker can forge its parameters, including PHP_ADMIN_VALUE settings like auto_prepend_file.

    View the interactive component on hafiz.dev.

    So the check is one grep. Is anything keeping FastCGI connections open?

    Industry observers note that no output on my server. fastcgi_keep_conn defaults to off, so every site there closes the connection after each request. The advisory also names Apache's mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on, HAProxy FastCGI backends and LSAPI. If you run any of those, this is the fix to apply first.

    Sources indicate that the Laravel side helps a little too. Symfony's Request::getContent() reads php://input to the end with file_get_contents(), unless you explicitly ask for a stream resource. But the advisory warns that reading the whole body may not be a reliable mitigation on its own. So the front end setting is the one I'd check.

    According to recent reports, the server uses Ondřej Surý's PPA, so the fix arrived as 16 php8.3 packages. I wanted three things. A way back, no surprise config changes, and proof afterwards that every PHP process was on the new binary.

    The dry run showed 16 upgrades, nothing new installed and nothing removed.

    The tail of the output had something I didn't ask for:.

    Industry observers note that ubuntu's needrestart saw that supervisor's children were running the old PHP binary and restarted supervisor on its own. That restarts every queue worker on the box. It's the right outcome (a worker on the old binary is still unpatched), but it happens mid-upgrade, whether or not a job is running. Laravel workers finish the current job when they get SIGTERM, as long as supervisor's stopwaitsecs is longer than your slowest job. I wrote about that in what happens to a running job when the worker stops. Check that setting before you patch, not after.

    According to recent reports, A process still on a replaced binary highlights up there with (deleted) after the path. Then I extracted the backup and ran diff -rq against /etc/php/8.3. Identical. Every site returned 200 before and after.

    One more detail from the verification. In October, after the previous session advisory, I'd added a one-line override for FPM:.

    In a recent development, the CLI has no such file. Its php.ini has the line commented out (;session.upload_progress.enabled = On), so the CLI uses PHP's compiled default. Before the upgrade, php -i on the CLI reported On. The upgrade kept php.ini byte for byte, as the diff confirmed.

    View the interactive component on hafiz.dev.

    In a recent development, the compiled default flipped. The serializer mismatch advisory says the fix disables session upload progress by default, and the binary agrees. The configuration page of the PHP manual still says it defaults to 1 at the time of writing, so don't trust the manual for this one. Trust php -i. I'm keeping the explicit Off for FPM anyway. A default can flip back on a rebuild, a different PPA or a different branch, and an explicit line in conf.d survives all of them.

    Nothing on my server uses upload progress, and in a Laravel app you probably don't either. Upload progress bars in the browser come from XHR's upload progress events, which need nothing from PHP. (I covered the Laravel side of massive uploads in handling large file uploads without crashing your server.).

    No. Laravel's session layer is its own Store class with its own drivers, and the framework never calls session_start(). That's why most of the ext-session fixes in this release don't reach Laravel code directly. The exception is upload progress, which PHP handles before any script runs.

    Yes, unless something on the server uses it, and Laravel apps rarely do. The fixed releases already default it to off, but an explicit session.upload_progress.enabled = Off in your FPM conf.d keeps it off whatever the default does later.

    In a recent development, yes. A long-running queue:work process keeps the old PHP binary in memory until it restarts. On Ubuntu, needrestart may restart supervisor for you during the upgrade, as it did for me. Elsewhere, restart them yourself, and make sure stopwaitsecs lets running jobs finish.

    Securing Laravel's notice before the release remarked Laravel would contact Forge, Cloud and Vapor owners with the steps. On Forge you still own the server, so check the PHP version yourself with php -v and php-fpm8.3 -v (or your version's binary) instead of assuming.

    None of this is a reason to wait. "My Laravel app doesn't reach it" is true for a clean server, and very few servers stay clean. A second site in the same FPM pool, a forgotten phpMyAdmin, someone enabling fastcgi_keep_conn for a benchmark next year. Each of those quietly turns a "no" in that table into a "yes".

    Recent findings suggest that what the analysis does tell you is where to look while you patch. Three checks cover most of it:.

    Sources indicate that the first finds persistent FastCGI connections. The second indicates the upload progress setting, where native sessions live, and whether startup warnings go to a file (the timezone bug needs that). The third tells you whether anything on the box uses native sessions at all.

    It has been revealed that my own answers were no keep-alive, upload progress off, and an empty session directory. error_log is unset, so startup warnings go to FPM's own log, which the timezone advisory says doesn't meet its condition. So the box wasn't exposed to the demonstrated attacks, and it's patched now regardless. The rest of that server's setup is in how I hardened my VPS with SSH keys, Cloudflare and Tailscale. For the dependency side of fast security fixes, see Composer 2.11's cooldown, which holds back security releases too.

    What I'm changing next is the one-pool-for-everything setup. With a separate FPM pool per site, a native session in one app can't leave freed memory for a request from another, and the interrupted shutdown bug would never have been a question.

    3 Dark Personality Traits Linked To Infidelity

    📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (428 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Org

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Certain personality traits may help explain why some people betray a partner’s trust.
    • Certain personality traits may help explain why some people betray a partner’s trust.
    • Psychopathy, manipulativeness and narcissism are all associated with cheating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Certain personality traits may help explain why some people betray a partner’s trust.

    Certain personality traits may help explain why some people betray a partner’s trust.

    Psychopathy, manipulativeness and narcissism are all associated with cheating.

    The strongest average link is with psychopathy, closely followed by Machiavellianism.

    Narcissism, which involves an inflated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration, has the weakest link.

    Impulsivity, emotional coldness and a willingness to manipulate others may help explain why these characteristics are associated with betrayal.

    The conclusions come from a review of 11 studies examining dark personality traits and infidelity.

    Participants included university students, married couples and adults from the general population.

    All three traits were positively associated with infidelity, although the strength of the association varied between studies.

    Psychopathic traits include impulsivity, low empathy and a lack of guilt.

    Someone with these characteristics may be more drawn to immediate sexual rewards and less concerned about hurting a partner.

    A willingness to take risks could also make the possibility of being caught less of a deterrent — impulsivity and deception may help explain this link.

    Psychopathy had the largest average correlation with cheating, although its association was close to that of Machiavellianism.

    Machiavellianism involves a cynical view of others and a willingness to manipulate people for personal advantage.

    In romantic relationships, these characteristics could make deception easier to justify when it serves someone’s interests.

    However, a calculating approach may also encourage caution.

    Someone concerned with protecting their reputation might weigh the potential rewards of an affair against the consequences of discovery.

    This calculated approach could help explain Machiavellianism’s slightly weaker link with cheating.

    Narcissism involves feelings of superiority, entitlement and a strong desire for admiration.

    Attention from another potential partner may appeal to someone who places great importance on being desirable.

    Nevertheless, narcissism had the smallest average association with infidelity and produced a less consistent pattern across the reviewed studies.

    An inflated ego alone therefore offers relatively little information about whether someone has been unfaithful.

    The broader picture may depend on how personality combines with relationship satisfaction, commitment and access to alternative partners.

    Dark traits provide only part of the explanation for why people betray a partner’s trust.

    The study was published in the journal Psihologija (Ataman & Yalçınkaya Alkar, 2025).

    Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean.

    Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

    📅 01 Jun 2022 | ⏱️ 4 min read (767 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Blogspot

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies.
    • In a recent development, an affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers.
    • Recent findings suggest that affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

    In a recent development, an affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

    Recent findings suggest that affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers. Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

    Sources indicate that dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

    In a recent development, performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

    Sources indicate that smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

    According to recent reports, the best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

    An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

    Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

    According to recent reports, A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program. Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

    Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

    Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:.

    One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

    Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:.

    Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

    Who manages your affiliate program?

    Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

    #137908. Industry News: TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

    📅 13 Jul 2022 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (980 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Blogspot ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

    📅 13 Jul 2022 | ⏱️ 5 min read (980 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Blogspot

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry.
    • According to recent reports, personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time.
    • Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

    According to recent reports, personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

    Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers.

    In a recent development, phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

    According to recent reports, hubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

    It has been revealed that when you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

    Acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include substantial brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and organization-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

    In a recent development, marketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool reveals you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for latest content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

    Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

    In a recent development, yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

    Industry observers note that albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

    Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

    It has been revealed that there are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

    Image by vectorjuice on FreepikIn this CJ Affiliate guide, I will share with you everything you need to get started on the platform, I will give you an in-depth look at the network and how it works.You will learn how to earn money with the platform. If you're not interested, I'll share some of the best CJ affiliate programs and alternatives. By the end of this post, I will also answer some of the FAQs on the platform and give my quick CJ review. Sounds Good So let’s startWhat is CJ Affiliate?Commission Junction is an online advertising company that offers affiliate programs for various retailers. Since 1998, it has been known as one of the oldest and most popular affiliate networks. Commission Junction has consistently ranked among the top 10 affiliate networks  With in-depth data analysis and an unmatched understanding of clients needs, CJ has established itself as a leader in performance marketing.For Advertiser:CJ provides advertisers with a variety of tracking, management, and payment options. As an affiliate network, CJ can help you launch multiple affiliate programs from a centralized network. CJ's experienced team of account managers is available to help at every step—from program set-up to optimization.For Publishers: CJ offers a  variety of well-paying affiliate programs. You can find affiliate programs in almost every niche at CJ. With CJ, you can also find promotional tools such as banners and product feeds, which help you promote your website. The reporting tools are unparalleled and provide granular data that can assist you in fine-tuning your campaigns for maximum results.Requirements First things first, CJ is free to join! If you are new to the world of affiliate marketing, don't worry—you'll be able to join right away. The requirements for joining CJ are almost similar to other networks. For example, you must have a blog or social media follower.Isn't it obvious? Let's explore the details.High-quality, unique content.Non-gated content, of course.Site privacy policy.No software, coupon/deal, or incentive modelsYour traffic must be from US and Canada. The main traffic source must not be paid10K+ monthly trafic on your website.How Does CJ Affiliate Work?Between advertisers and publishers, CJ Affiliate acts as a middleman.. Advertisers sign up on CJ to promote their products or services, while publishers sign up on CJ to find and join affiliate programs to make money. CJ then tracks the sales or leads generated by the publisher and pays them a commission according to the terms of the affiliate program.CJ provides a win-win situation for both sides: advertisers get more sales and publishers make money. In order to free up both parties to concentrate on their job, CJ also handles payments and other technical issues. Now that you know how CJ works, let's learn more about how to sign up and start making money with it.How to Start Making Money Online Using CJ AffiliateTo get started using CJ's affiliate network, you'll need to register for an account. To do this, you must have a website or social media profile with relevant content and an audience from the US or Canada. Create a CJ account, complete the application process, and then wait for approval. You shouldn't worry CJ is not strict as other network in approving applications.Here's how you can signup for Cj Visit cj.com to register as a publisher. Fill in information such as your nationality, email, password, and more.Verify your email address now.You will be transferred right away to your CJ Account Manager, which contains crucial data including network statistics and performance summaries.Now from the Account menu, head to Network Profile. And to sign up for any affiliate programme offered on CJ, complete this profile separately.When applying for CJ, you need to share these two pieces of information Description of the website (include statistics for your site and more)Promotion methods (Traffic sources)The process of setting up a CJ Affiliate account is a way for you to prove to CJ and the merchants that you're a serious affiliate marketer. Your CJ account is complete once you've added or edited your payment information; now you need to add or edit your tax certificates if required. You are now prepared to start making money on CJ Affiliate program apply for product when approved start promting and earn commissions on every sale.Click on "Advertisers" and then select a category to go to  your niche advertiser area. You can apply for it by clicking the 'Join the Program' button and analysing three months' earnings per click and overall earnings! After you're approved, you'll get links from all over the Internet.After you've completed the steps above, you can share your affiliate links in your blog post. You can view performance reports for your affiliate links by visiting the CJ account dashboard. Click "Clients" to see details about clicks, sales, and commissions earned by each client.With CJ, you can make money promoting great products and services in any niche imaginable! So start joining CJ programs now and watch your business grow.Best CJ Affiliate Programs in 2022On CJ, you can find thousands of affiliate programs in almost any niche. Some of the top affiliate programs enlisted on CJ include:Contabo VPS Fiverr Hostinger Godaddy Namecheap You'll find a lot of programs to join at CJ, depending on your niche. Just enter your keywords in the search bar, and CJ will show you all the relevant programs that match your criteria. You can further filter the results by commission type, category, or country.A Quick CJ Affiliate Review: Is It Good Enough? CJ Affiliate is one of the oldest and most well-known affiliate networks. The platform has been around for over 20 years and has a massive network of advertisers and publishers. The features on CJ Affiliate are easy to use, and it offers advertisers a wide range of tracking, management, and payment options. CJ offers some great features for publishers too—promotional tools like banners, links, and social media are available to help boost your site's visibility. The only downside is that CJ has a bit of a learning curve, and the approval process can be strict. But overall, CJ Affiliate is an excellent platform for advertisers and publishers. Top Alternatives and CompetitorsCJ Affiliate is a great place to earn an income from affiliate marketing. It offers a wide range of features and options for advertisers and publishers. But if CJ doesn't work for you, plenty of other options are available. Here are some of the top competitors and alternatives in the market today:ShareASaleAWINImpact Rakuten MarketingPartnerStack Partnerize ClickBank Here are some of the best CJ Affiliate alternatives that you can try. Each platform has its own set of features, so make sure to choose one that best suits your needs. Regardless of which CJ alternative you choose, remember that quality content is key to success as a publisher, so ensure to focus on providing high-value, engaging content to your readers.Frequently Asked Questions About Cj Affiliate Marketplace Is the Cj AffilIs late Network legit?CJ Affiliate is a legitimate affiliate platform that has earned the trust of many marketers because of its vast network of advertisers and publishers.How much do CJ affiliates make?It's not just about CJ; it's about how much effort you put into making money. It is possible to earn a few dollars to a few thousand dollars How much does it cost to join Cj?Joining CJ is free of charge. There are no monthly or annual fees. You only pay when you make a sale, and CJ takes a commission of 5-10%.What are the payment methods accepted by Cj?You can receive payment via direct deposit or check, as well as through Payoneer. CJ pays out within 20 days of the end of the month if your account has at least $50 worth of deposits ($100 for those outside America).How to get approved for CJ affiliate?CJ is friendly to both beginners and advanced affiliates. You need a website or social media profile with a solid organic traffic source and make yourself known using your profile description. Be honest, and you'll get approved for CJ's affiliate network. How to find programs on CJ affiliates?CJ affiliate offers a straightforward and user-friendly interface. All you need is to log in to your CJ account and click on ‘Advertisers' from the menu. Depending on your niche, you can then search for any affiliate program on CJ What are the Pros of CJ Affiliate for advertisers?CJ Affiliate is one of the most advanced affiliate programs available, providing advertisers with a range of features and options including advanced tracking, management, and payment options. The platform is also easy to use and provides promotional tools like coupons, banners, and widgets that can help increase our sales.Final Saying Choosing Commission Junction as your affiliate program isn't easy. CJ is a major company and they have a wide range of affiliates, big and small. They offer everything from banner ads to text links and so much more. The sheer amount of choices can seem intimidating at first, especially to new Affiliates, which is why we've put together this simple guide for people looking for a successful CJ affiliate program to join. If you have any questions feel free to ask in the comments.

    In this article, we explore the top 10 AI tools that are driving innovation and efficiency in various industries. These tools are designed to automate repetitive tasks, improve workflow, and increase productivity. The tools included in our list are some of the most advanced and widely used in the market, and are suitable for a variety of applications. Some of the tools focus on natural language processing, such as ChatGPT and Grammarly, while others focus on image and video generation, such as DALL-E and Lumen5. Other tools such as OpenAI Codex, Tabnine, Canva, Jasper AI,, and Surfer SEO are designed to help with specific tasks such as code understanding content writing and website optimization. This list is a great starting point for anyone looking to explore the possibilities of AI and how it can be applied to their business or project. So let’s dive into 1. ChatGPT ChatGPT is a large language model that generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts. It can be used for tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion. It can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing, and generates coherent and fluent text, but should be used with care as it may generate text that is biased, offensive, or factually incorrect. Pros: Generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts Can be fine-tuned for specific tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion Can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing Can generate coherent and fluent text, even when completing a given text prompt. Cons: May generate text that is biased or offensive Can generate text that is not accurate or factually correct May require large amounts of computational resources to run The model can sometimes generate text that is not coherent or fluent, depending on the prompt given. Overall, ChatGPT is a powerful tool for natural language processing, but it should be used with care and with an understanding of its limitations. 2. DALL-E DALL-E is a generative model developed by OpenAI that is capable of generating images from text prompts. It is based on the GPT-3 architecture, which is a transformer-based neural network language model that has been trained on a massive dataset of text. DALL-E can generate images that are similar to a training dataset and it can generate high-resolution images that are suitable for commercial use. Pros: Generates high-resolution images Can generate images from text prompts It can be fine-tuned for specific tasks such as generating images of a certain style or category Cons: May generate images that are not entirely original and could be influenced by the training data May require significant computational resources to run The quality of the generated images may vary depending on the specific prompt Overall, DALL-E is a powerful AI-based tool for generating images, it can be used for a variety of applications such as creating images for commercial use, gaming, and other creative projects. It is key to note that the generated images should be reviewed and used with care, as they may not be entirely original and could be influenced by the training data. 3. Lumen5 Lumen5 is a content creation platform that uses AI to help users create videos, social media posts, and other types of content. It has several features that make it useful for content creation and marketing, including: Pros: Automatically summarizes text from a blog post, article, or another source into a script for a video or social media post Offers a library of royalty-free videos, images, and music to use in content Has a drag-and-drop interface for easy content creation Can create videos in multiple languages Has a built-in analytics tool to track the performance of created content. Cons: The quality of the generated content may vary depending on the source material The automatic summarization feature may not always capture the main points of the source material The library of videos, images, and music is limited. The analytics feature is basic Overall, Lumen5 is a useful tool for creating content quickly and easily, it can help automate the process of creating videos, social media posts, and other types of content. However, the quality of the generated content may vary depending on the source material and it is important to review and edit the content before publishing it. 4. Grammarly Grammarly is a writing-enhancement platform that uses AI to check for grammar, punctuation, and spelling errors in the text. It also provides suggestions for improving the clarity, concision, and readability of the text. It has several features that make it useful for improving writing, including: Pros: Checks for grammar, punctuation, and spelling errors in the text Provides suggestions for improving clarity, concision, and readability Can be integrated with various apps and platforms such as Microsoft Office, Google Docs, and social media platforms Offers a browser extension and a desktop app Has a premium version with more advanced features such as plagiarism detection and more Cons: The suggestions provided may not always be accurate or appropriate The grammar checker may not always recognize context-specific language use The free version has limited features Limited to English language only Overall, Grammarly is a useful tool for improving writing, it can help users identify and correct grammar and punctuation errors, and improve the clarity, concision, and readability of their text. However, it is important to review the suggestions provided by the tool and use them with caution, as they may not always be accurate or appropriate. 5.OpenAI Codex OpenAI Codex is a system developed by OpenAI that can create code from natural language descriptions of software tasks. The system is based on the GPT-3 model and can generate code in multiple programming languages. Pros: Can automate the process of writing code Can help developers to be more productive Can help non-technical people to create software Can generate code in multiple programming languages Cons: The quality of the generated code may vary depending on the task description The generated code may not always be optimal or efficient The system may not be able to handle complex software tasks Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the code. Overall, OpenAI Codex is a powerful tool that can help automate the process of writing code and make it more accessible to non-technical people. However, the quality of the generated code may vary depending on the task description and it is important to review and test the code before using it in a production environment. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the developer's knowledge. 6. Tabnine Tabnine is a code completion tool that uses AI to predict and suggest code snippets. It is compatible with multiple programming languages and can be integrated with various code editors. Pros: Can improve coding efficiency by suggesting code snippets based on context Can complete entire code blocks Can predict variables, functions, and other elements of code Can be integrated with various code editors Cons: The suggestions may not always be accurate or appropriate The system may not always be able to understand the context of the code May not work with all code editors Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the code. Overall, TabNine is a useful tool for developers that can help improve coding efficiency and reduce the time spent on writing code. However, it is important to review the suggestions provided by the tool and use them with caution, as they may not always be accurate or appropriate. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the developer's knowledge. 7. Jasper AI Jasper is a content writing and content generation tool that uses artificial intelligence to identify the best words and sentences for your writing style and medium in the most efficient, quick, and accessible way. Pros: User-friendly interface Generates a wide variety of content types Guarantees 100% unique and free-plagiarism content SEO friendly  Create articles of up to 10k words Cons: Not the cheapest AI writer on the market 8. Surfer SEO Surfer SEO is a software tool designed to help website owners and digital marketers improve their search engine optimization (SEO) efforts. The tool provides a variety of features that can be used to analyze a website's on-page SEO, including: Features: A site audit tool that checks for technical SEO concerns A content editor that suggests optimizations for individual pages A keyword research tool that suggests keywords to target A SERP analyzer that highlights how a website's pages rank for specific keywords A backlink analysis tool that shows the backlinks pointing to a website. Pros: Can help website owners and marketers identify technical SEO issues Can provide suggestions for optimizing individual pages Can help with keyword research Can show how a website's pages rank for specific keywords Can provide insight into a website's backlink profile Cons: Some features may require a paid subscription The tool is not a guarantee of better ranking The tool can only analyze the data it has access to The tool's suggestions may not always be applicable or optimal Overall, Surfer SEO can be a useful tool for website owners and digital marketers looking to improve their SEO efforts. However, it is important to remember that it is just a tool and should be used in conjunction with other SEO best practices. Additionally, the tool is not a guarantee of better ranking. 9. Zapier Zapier is a web automation tool that allows users to automate repetitive tasks by connecting different web applications together. It does this by creating "Zaps" that automatically move data between apps, and can also be used to trigger certain actions in one app based on events in another app. Features: Can connect over 3,000 web applications Can automate repetitive tasks Can create "Zaps" to move data between apps Can trigger certain actions in one app based on events in another app. Pros: Can automate repetitive tasks Can save time Can improve workflow Can increase productivity Can be integrated with a wide range of web applications Cons: Can be difficult to set up May require some technical skills May require a paid subscription for some features Some apps may not be compatible Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the apps Overall, Zapier is a useful tool that can help users automate repetitive tasks and improve workflow. It can save time and increase productivity by connecting different web applications together. However, it may require some technical skills and some features may require a paid subscription. It is important to use the tool with caution and not to rely too much on it, to understand the apps better. 10. Compose AI Compose AI is a company that specializes in developing natural language generation (NLG) software. Their software uses AI to automatically generate written or spoken text from structured data, such as spreadsheets, databases, or APIs. Features: Automatically generates written or spoken text from structured data Can be integrated with a wide range of data sources Can be used for a variety of applications such as creating reports, summaries, and explanations Provides an API and a user-friendly interface Pros: Can automate the process of creating written or spoken content Can help users create more accurate and consistent content Can help users save time by automating repetitive tasks Can be integrated with a wide range of data sources Cons: The quality of the generated content may vary depending on the data source The generated content may not always be optimal or efficient The system may not be able to handle complex tasks Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the data Overall, Compose AI's NLG software can be a useful tool for automating the process of creating written or spoken content from structured data. However, the quality of the generated content may vary depending on the data source, and it is essential to review the generated content before using it in a production environment. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the understanding of the data. Conclusion AI tools are becoming increasingly important in today's business and technology landscape.     Industry observers note that the essence of the best grilled cheese lies in the delicious combination of melted cheese and crisped bread. There are many methods to accomplish such a pairing, with plenty of tips to give you the best results imaginable. If you're after a version that's especially ooey-gooey, try making the sandwich with cheddar cheese spread.

    Sources indicate that available from several brands at widespread grocery stores like Walmart, cheddar cheese spread is essentially cheddar mixed with butter. The foodstuff is easily spreadable on bread and melts when it's heated, making a grilled cheese with a pleasantly runny interior. While it's creamier than classic cheddar, the flavor is no afterthought, with this cheese's sharpness still perceptible.

    Recent findings suggest that using butter alongside cheese is common in grilled cheese recipes; the spread lets you conveniently lather on both components at once. The fat enhances the bread's crispiness, all while retaining a moist interior. As a sole filling, the spread turns the dish luxuriously decadent — but complemented with a few slices of cheese, it's a grilled cheese rendition to remember.

    There are many international grilled cheese styles to explore; cheddar cheese spread fits into a wide range of renditions. Combined with a store-bought loaf of sourdough and sliced cheddar, the spread makes a mouth-watering classic. However, you can consider layering in other ingredients, too — thereby making a cheddar grilled cheese with a twist.

    For example, the cheese's sharpness welcomes a sweet contrast. Spread a jam or jelly into the sandwich, whether a rich fig jam, tart cranberry preserves, or a sweet blackberry jam. For a sweet touch with less sugar, you could also use fresh fruits to upgrade any grilled cheese; the spread would go great with apples, for example, as apples and cheddar are a match made in sandwich heaven. And you could also consider leaning into the spice, smearing on spicy brown mustard or hot pepper jelly for a light dose of heat.

    It has been revealed that consider trying out other ingredient add-ins, too. Caramelized onions will lend a grilled cheese a subtle nutty sweetness, while bacon bits bring a savory touch. Cheddar cheese spreads allow the many different flavors to come together, letting you easily craft a sandwich to your tastes.

    📅 05 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (444 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Org ↗ Open Full Page

    The Vitamin Deficiency Linked To Chronic Headaches

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (444 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Org

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Almost four in five people with chronic migraine have low levels of this vitamin.
    • Almost four in five people with chronic migraine have low levels of this vitamin.
    • Frequent headaches are linked to lower vitamin D levels.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Almost four in five people with chronic migraine have low levels of this vitamin.

    Almost four in five people with chronic migraine have low levels of this vitamin.

    Frequent headaches are linked to lower vitamin D levels.

    People with chronic migraine have lower levels than those with occasional migraines or no headache disorder.

    Lower vitamin D is also associated with greater muscle tenderness.

    The vitamin helps muscles and nerves function, making it relevant to understanding pain.

    One possibility is that low levels amplify sensitivity to pain, although this remains an explanation to investigate.

    The research compared around 150 adults, divided equally between chronic migraine, episodic migraine and a group without headache disorders.

    Blood tests showed low vitamin D in 78 percent of the chronic migraine group, compared with 60 percent of those with episodic migraine and 46 percent of the comparison group.

    Average levels were lowest in chronic migraine and highest among those without headaches.

    Chronic migraine means headaches on at least 15 days a month for more than three months, with migraine features on at least eight days.

    These headaches can change in character, even within the same day, and can include pain resembling tension headaches.

    Lower vitamin D levels were associated with more tenderness when muscles were pressed.

    The researchers suggest that muscular discomfort and changes in pain processing could interact, potentially helping sustain headaches.

    However, the association could also run in the opposite direction: people with migraine may spend less time outdoors because of light sensitivity or fatigue.

    The findings do not establish that supplements prevent migraines.

    Vitamin D’s established functions extend beyond maintaining strong bones.

    It helps the body absorb calcium, supports muscle movement and allows nerves to carry messages between the brain and the body.

    Deficiency can cause a condition called osteomalacia in adults, involving bone pain and muscle weakness.

    The body produces vitamin D when sunlight reaches the skin, while food provides another source.

    Oily fish, including salmon and mackerel, are among the best natural sources, while egg yolks contain smaller amounts.

    Some breakfast cereals and other foods are fortified with the vitamin.

    People who rarely expose their skin to sunlight can have more difficulty obtaining enough.

    A blood test measures vitamin D status, helping distinguish a nutritional shortage from symptoms with other possible explanations.

    The study was published in the journal Cephalalgia Reports (Prakash et al., 2026).

    Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean.
