    #137877. 22 Recipes To Make With Thanksgiving Leftovers

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2580 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    22 Recipes To Make With Thanksgiving Leftovers

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2580 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Turkey, ham, mashed potatoes, casseroles, pumpkin, cranberries, stuffing ...
    • Sources indicate that especially when you're hosting a crowd (which is possible to do stress-free with these tips from Guy Fieri), those leftovers can be abundant.
    • It has been revealed that if you're looking for new ideas or creative ways to use up what's left in the fridge, we've got a plethora of recipes to try that'll help you make the most of your Thanksgiving leftovers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Turkey, ham, mashed potatoes, casseroles, pumpkin, cranberries, stuffing ... the annual fall-flavored feast that we know and love is always a crowd-pleasing holiday meal to look forward to. And one of the best things about Thanksgiving isn't just the meal itself; it's all of the delicious leftovers that inevitably follow.

    Sources indicate that especially when you're hosting a crowd (which is possible to do stress-free with these tips from Guy Fieri), those leftovers can be abundant. But the beauty is that there's so much more you can do with your Thanksgiving leftovers than just reheat and re-eat. From soups, sandwiches, and snacks that repurpose your ingredients to completely fresh dishes that transform the original elements of the meal, you can take those leftovers in so many directions.

    It has been revealed that if you're looking for new ideas or creative ways to use up what's left in the fridge, we've got a plethora of recipes to try that'll help you make the most of your Thanksgiving leftovers. (Pro tip: Just don't forget the 2-2-2 rule with your leftovers to ensure food safety.).

    Industry observers note that whether you enjoyed some mac & cheese on Thanksgiving Day or not, this recipe is a whole new twist on the classic that infuses the beloved dish with holiday flavor. It's honestly a little shocking how many leftover ingredients manage to make their way into this one recipe, but when you think about it ... how could it not taste good?

    It has been revealed that this Thanksgiving Leftover Macaroni & Cheese incorporates three different types of cheese — fontina, cheddar, and mascarpone — to make the cheese sauce. Then come the Thanksgiving leftovers that get folded into the dish: shredded turkey meat, sweet potatoes, peas, and pasta. After it's baked, the whole thing is topped off with some cranberry sauce to bring the Thanksgiving flavors home.

    Recipe: Thanksgiving Leftover Macaroni & Cheese.

    Industry observers note that now, this is a fun one — it's Thanksgiving dinner in burger form! Not only can you use that leftover stuffing, but this recipe also calls for turkey meat, gravy, and cranberry sauce, so this one wins for maximizing whatever's taking up space in the fridge. And it's incredibly tasty, too.

    Sources indicate that the "burger" is a combination of stuffing, turkey, eggs, and milk in patty form. The patty is then griddled in some butter and topped off with cranberry sauce, gravy, and goat cheese to create a burger that'll leave you stuffed in the best way.

    Recipe: Leftover Thanksgiving Stuffing Burger.

    Okay, a turkey cheesesteak might seem a little contradictory, but this one's worth entertaining when it comes to making the most of your Thanksgiving leftovers. You won't just knock out the leftover turkey, but also any leftover gravy with this Thanksgiving Leftover Turkey Cheesesteak.

    Recent findings suggest that the cheesesteak starts with sautéed sweet onions, and then the turkey (dark meat works great if you have it), gravy, and cornichons are added to the mix before two types of cheese (provolone and American cheese) are melted on top. Everything is stuffed into toasty hoagie rolls to make a saucy, messy, tasty Thanksgiving cheesesteak.

    Recipe: Thanksgiving Leftover Turkey Cheesesteak.

    Sources indicate that why not whip up the ultimate comfort meal to enjoy the weekend after Thanksgiving? Once the holiday winds down, you can use your leftover turkey (and any extra pumpkin puree you might have lying around) in this Pumpkin and Turkey Chili recipe. This fall take on a classic slow cooker chili recipe incorporates pumpkin puree into the stew along with a blend of warm spices like cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg.

    To sub in your already-cooked turkey, just skip the initial step where you'd brown the ground turkey, and instead add some cubed or shredded turkey once your chili is simmering.

    Recipe: Pumpkin and Turkey Chili.

    Making croquettes is a fun and delicious way to use up that leftover turkey. Croquettes actually originated in France as a way to use up leftover meats and vegetables, so they're the perfect way to repurpose those Thanksgiving leftovers.

    Sources indicate that the cheesy croquettes are made by sautéeing mushrooms, onions, and garlic and combining the mixture with cooked turkey, parsley, and mozzarella cheese. They're then shaped into balls, dipped into egg and breadcrumbs, and lightly fried until golden brown and crispy.

    Recipe: Crispy Turkey and Cheese Croquettes.

    According to recent reports, shepherd's pie is a great follow-up recipe to Thanksgiving if you need a way to reuse copious amounts of mashed potatoes, because that iconic mashed potato topping makes shepherd's pie what it is. This particular recipe is made with ground lamb and vegetables like corn, peas, and carrots as the base of the pie, but you could easily sub in your leftover turkey as well if you want to knock out two leftovers in one go.

    It has been revealed that either way, this Simple Shepherd's Pie is even easier to make since the mashed potatoes are already done. All you need to do is assemble, bake, and enjoy ... or if you're feeling ambitious, you can try one of these 15 secret ingredients to make your Shepherd's Pie the best it can be.

    Recent findings suggest that bought too many potatoes on your Thanksgiving grocery run? This casserole will come in handy for those extra ingredients. The simple, easy-to-make dish combines potatoes, onions, bacon, and thyme with cream, chicken stock, and cheese. Everything gets baked until it's melty and delicious, making a perfect side dish to pair with any leftover meat from the holiday.

    This recipe uses blue cheese, which complements the bacon, but you can feel free to use any cheese you like (cheddar, mozzarella, or even Gruyère would all work great).

    Recipe: Potato Bacon Cheese Bake.

    In a recent development, this comforting soup brings together many ingredients that were most likely on your Thanksgiving shopping list, including carrots, apples, potatoes, and pecans. It's the perfect meal to throw together that'll make use of all of those extra groceries that you're not sure what to do with. Carrots and apples may not be your first thoughts as the base of a soup, but trust us, this comforting soup recipe is a (somewhat unexpected) winner.

    All you need to do is cook your vegetables down with plenty of flavorful herbs and spices like cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and fresh thyme. Add your stock, blend until smooth, and finish off with the cream for a nutty and rich yet soothing soup that you can work your way through all week.

    Recipe: Nutty Carrot and Apple Soup.

    Recent findings suggest that for all those who may have purchased some fresh pumpkins for your Thanksgiving pie but didn't get around to using all of it, we've got just the recipe. As a bonus, it'll use up those extra potatoes, too!

    According to recent reports, put a fall spin on a classic potato gratin by slicing your pumpkin into pieces or rounds the same size as your potatoes. The cream mixture, which is made up of heavy cream, garlic, thyme, rosemary, and salt, gets layered with your pumpkin and potatoes; then everything is covered with grated Swiss cheese and baked longer than you may think until the whole dish is bubbly, browned, and cheesy.

    Recipe: Herbed Pumpkin Potato Gratin.

    It has been revealed that whether you've got some extra sweet potatoes lying around from a casserole side dish or a sweet potato pie, this Sweet Potato Tarte Tatin is a delicious way to use them up. And with a little puff pastry, this dish looks impressive but doesn't take long to make a classic tarte tatin.

    Recent findings suggest that the trick is making the caramel element; once you've gotten that down, the rest is smooth sailing. Your homemade caramel will come together with sliced sweet potatoes and a puff pastry covering to produce an irresistible starchy take on the tarte tatin.

    Recipe: Sweet Potato Tarte Tatin.

    Similar to the tarte tatin, you can use a store-bought dough (this time, paper-thin Greek phyllo pastry) to keep this dessert simple. Baklava is typically made with nuts, but this recipe replaces that crunchy ingredient with a smooth pumpkin puree — along with spices like cinnamon, nutmeg, and clove — for a tasty fall twist on this decadent, flaky treat.

    Baklava involves making a simple syrup of sorts, and then it's all about layering (and this hack for assembling can make your baklava process even quicker). In the end, you'll have an extremely crispy, sweet-yet-spiced dessert born from leftover pumpkin puree.

    It has been revealed that if there's one thing you may not have thought to do with your leftover pumpkin and cranberries, it might be homemade liqueur. It might seem a little extreme, but it's not as complicated as it sounds, and you will be rewarded with an ingredient that'll help level up your baking and cocktails for many weeks to come.

    In short, the process just involves cooking down your chosen ingredient with sugar, then adding a high-proof liquor like vodka, and then straining it and letting it sit. That's it!

    Recipe: Cranberry Liqueur and Pumpkin Liqueur.

    According to recent reports, if you didn't quite make as much apple pie filling as you planned, don't worry — this one's for you. It's basically a shortcut apple pie filling that you can throw on some ice cream, douse in whipped cream, or simply enjoy on its own.

    This Sweet Spiced Baked Apples recipe is one of the easiest ways to make use of all of those leftover apples. Any apples will do: Honeycrisp, Fuji, Pink Lady, you name it. All you need to do is bake them with an undeniably delicious mixture of brown sugar, walnuts, butter, and spices. It's so simple, and so satisfying.

    Recipe: Sweet Spiced Baked Apples.

    In a recent development, sticking with those leftover apples, this recipe will make a fantastic breakfast or brunch in the days following Thanksgiving. The Americanized origins of Dutch baby pancakes are a bit complicated, but long story short, this creation is essentially a giant, skillet-baked pancake. And it's a great go-to dish to capitalize on your extra apples, because you most likely have everything else you need stocked in your kitchen.

    In a recent development, this Dutch baby recipe uses a batter made of flour, milk, eggs, honey, vanilla extract, salt, and melted butter. Next, pour the batter over thinly sliced apples that have been tossed in brown sugar and cinnamon. Everything is then baked together to perfection until your leftover apples turn into puffy, golden goodness.

    This is a unique and flavorful way to use any extra pumpkins you have from the holiday. The bonus? The presentation is impressive, so if you find yourself continuing to host through the weekend, this is another great meal to provide for your guests that will help you repurpose some of your Thanksgiving ingredients.

    With everything from coconut milk and ground pork to ginger, soy sauce, and water chestnuts, this rice dish includes a lot of really interesting ingredients that may not seem like they belong together, but they all unite to build a warm, aromatic meal. Just trust the process, serve it up inside a pumpkin, and watch your guests marvel.

    Recipe: Stuffed Pumpkin With Aromatic Rice.

    Although this recipe includes a lot of similar ingredients as the above (rice, pumpkin, nuts), the elements come together in a totally different way to create a totally different dish: a warmly spiced, sweet rice pudding that'll taste just like your Thanksgiving pumpkin pie.

    The dessert is made with Arborio rice, almond milk, maple syrup, pumpkin puree, vanilla, and spices — everything gets simmered together until it thickens into a pudding, then chilled and served with glazed pecans for extra crunch.

    Recipe: Vegan Pumpkin Pecan Rice Pudding.

    In a recent development, leftovers truly shine when you use them to build a great sandwich. Meet this Sweet and Savory Monte Cristo Sandwich, which can be made with your leftover Thanksgiving turkey and ham. In addition to the sliced duo of meat, this sandwich features Gruyère cheese, mayo, and raspberry jam (although you can obviously sub in some cranberry sauce if you so please), all stacked between slices of brioche bread.

    In a recent development, what makes this Monte Cristo extra delicious is the French toast treatment that it gets: Once assembled, the entire sandwich is dipped in a mixture of egg, half-and-half, and nutmeg and lightly fried in butter until golden brown. Oh, it's then topped off with some powdered sugar for good measure.

    Recipe: Sweet And Savory Monte Cristo Sandwich.

    Recent findings suggest that here's another fun breakfast recipe to keep things interesting over the holiday weekend! This take on a Croque Madame (a classic French sandwich typically made with ham, cheese, and Mornay sauce and topped with a sunny-side-up egg) creates a "waffled" version of the sandwich by employing a waffle iron as the cooking tool.

    Where do the leftovers come in? The waffle "batter" is made with your leftover Thanksgiving stuffing, which you'll then combine with milk and eggs. This concoction is then topped with slices of ham and grated cheddar cheese, and finished off with a fried or poached egg. Post-Thanksgiving brunch is served.

    According to recent reports, if you've still got some sweet potatoes left from your holiday shopping, this is another great recipe to make use of them — and it couldn't be simpler. This Sweet Potato and Sausage Hash makes a great breakfast or brunch, and can be topped with some eggs or eaten on its own. And all it takes is six ingredients to get there.

    It has been revealed that the dish starts with some onions and garlic sautéed in butter. These are then combined with cooked Italian sausage and cubed sweet potatoes. Everything is roasted together in a cast-iron skillet, showing how you can make this recipe with minimal effort and maximum tastiness.

    Recipe: Sweet Potato and Sausage Hash.

    According to recent reports, there are never enough ways to use up those extra potatoes! This time, your floury potatoes like Yukon Golds or Russets take the lead with an herby potato galette. This particular recipe is a crustless galette, so there's no dough necessary, and you only need a handful of ingredients to make it.

    In a recent development, to make the galette, shred the potatoes, add them to a hot skillet with lots of olive oil and sage, then press them down to help form a natural crust. Cook the potatoes for another 10 minutes as butter is added to the pan, then flip the whole thing and cook it on the other side. The result is a crispy potato pancake that's golden on the outside, soft on the inside, and delicious all the way around.

    Recipe: Potato Galettes With Sage.

    It has been revealed that it's the ultimate Thanksgiving grilled cheese, so you don't want to pass this one up. You can make use of several leftover ingredients for this sandwich, both savory and sweet, such as extra apples and leftover ham.

    Apple butter is spread across two slices of sourdough bread, and then layered with Brie, diced ham, and diced apples before the sandwich is toasted in butter. This simply isn't your average grilled cheese sandwich; you also get bonus points if you can pair it with some butternut squash soup.

    Recipe: Sweet and Savory Brie and Apple Butter Grilled Cheese.

    The State With The Most Wendy's Locations Isn't Fresh York, California, Or Texas

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (476 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Wendy's is a beloved chain of fast food restaurants whose square-shaped burger patties are instantly recognizable to many American diners.
    • Recent findings suggest that the Sunshine State accounts for roughly 8% of the total number of locations this fast food giant has in the United States, compared to Texas, which has slightly fewer locations at 419.
    • Additionally, two Florida cities — Miami and Orlando — are in the top five U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Wendy's is a beloved chain of fast food restaurants whose square-shaped burger patties are instantly recognizable to many American diners. Founded in 1969 in Columbus, Ohio, the brand is an institution where it was born — yet the Midwestern state doesn't actually have the most locations. Neither do populous hubs like California or Fresh York. Rather, you need to look southeast to the land of orange groves. With 464 restaurants as of November 2026, Florida has more Wendy's locations than any other state in the country.

    Recent findings suggest that the Sunshine State accounts for roughly 8% of the total number of locations this fast food giant has in the United States, compared to Texas, which has slightly fewer locations at 419. However, if you take population differences into account, there are more restaurants per capita in Florida than in the Lone Star State. This means that Florida residents are more likely to find a Wendy's nearby. Not everything seems to be bigger in Texas, after all, at least when it comes to this fast food chain.

    Additionally, two Florida cities — Miami and Orlando — are in the top five U.S. cities with the most Wendy's locations (per ScrapeHero). So, whether you're enjoying the nightlife of South Beach or visiting Disney World, you won't be too far from a Jr. Bacon Cheeseburger. Despite Florida's distinction of having the most locations, however, it doesn't have the largest Wendy's in the world. That honor goes to Tbilisi, the capital of Georgia, a country in the Caucasus region.

    The idea of people vacationing in, moving to, or spending part of the year in Florida is an old trope, and there's a good reason for it. Many Americans see the state as a respite from the cold, and the Sunshine State actually has a long history of being a destination for migrants moving down from northern states, dating back to as early as the 1800s.

    Interestingly, people from Ohio comprise a large portion of these migrants — in fact, according to USAFacts, more Ohioans moved to Florida than to any other state in 2024. Just like immigrants from other countries, American transplants bring their own cultures that can influence the local culinary scene, and maybe that's why there are so many Wendy's locations in the Sunshine State.

    According to recent reports, considering how the brand was founded in the Buckeye State, perhaps the many transplants brought their taste for the chain's iconic baked potatoes, chili, and square burgers with them. After all, Ohio has the third-largest number of Wendy's restaurants and has more locations per capita than Florida. It might seem like mere coincidence until you take into account the fact that Florida is also home to another Buckeye institution, Skyline Chili, and it's the only state outside the Midwest where the chain is present.

    #137864. Crostata Di Mele (Italian Apple Pie) Recipe

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1255 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Crostata Di Mele (Italian Apple Pie) Recipe

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1255 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • While working as a young pastry chef in an Italian trattoria, I had the great fortune of spending 3 weeks eating my way through Italy in an attempt to discover the most unique and tempting desserts each region had to offer.
    • Recent findings suggest that my recipe for crostata di Mele (Italian apple pie) is a bakery-worthy homage to those delightful desserts, and it became a seasonal fixture on my pastry menu.
    • It has been revealed that learning how to make the dough and filling for this crostata will give you a solid foundation for making other Italian pastries.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    While working as a young pastry chef in an Italian trattoria, I had the great fortune of spending 3 weeks eating my way through Italy in an attempt to discover the most unique and tempting desserts each region had to offer. Although I tasted complex and ethereal cakes, pastries, and frozen delights, I kept coming back to the simple fruit crostatas: buttery crusts molded into tart pans or baked free-form in rustic rounds, topped with glistening fruits and cakey or custardy fillings. These desserts tasted like perfection in their simplicity and purity of flavors.

    Recent findings suggest that my recipe for crostata di Mele (Italian apple pie) is a bakery-worthy homage to those delightful desserts, and it became a seasonal fixture on my pastry menu. A traditional pasta frolla (Italian short dough) crust is filled with a lemon and vanilla-scented creme patissiere (pastry cream custard) and topped with tart, crisp apples and crunchy turbinado sugar. The warm crostata is given a finishing glaze of melted apricot preserves, then chilled for serving.

    It has been revealed that learning how to make the dough and filling for this crostata will give you a solid foundation for making other Italian pastries. The dough is easy to work with, and the pastry cream is a versatile filling for other treats, such as profiteroles, layer cakes, or napoleons.

    There are 3 main components in the crostata di mele: the crust, the custard filling, and the toppings. For the crust, you will need all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, sea salt, cold unsalted butter, a large egg plus 1 yolk, vanilla extract, and the zest of a large lemon. The difference between this crostata dough and regular apple pie dough is the addition of eggs, which makes the dough slightly less flaky but more pliable for rolling and shaping. For the pastry cream, you will need whole milk, a vanilla bean, more lemon zest, 4 yolks, granulated sugar, and cornstarch. You will split the vanilla bean lengthwise to release the tiny black seeds into the milk, and the cornstarch acts as a thickening agent. To top the crostata, I like using apples that are crisp and tart, but that also have a balance of sweetness. Honeycrisp, Pink Lady, and Granny Smith are perfect apple varieties for this recipe. You will toss your apple slices with fresh lemon juice to prevent browning before baking, and use some melted butter to secure a crunchy sprinkling of turbinado sugar. To give your baked crostata a shiny finish, you will need apricot preserves to melt down and strain.

    Combine the flour, sugar, and salt in a stand mixer bowl.

    Add the butter a few pieces at a time and mix until pea-sized clumps form.

    Add the egg, yolk, lemon zest, and vanilla, and mix until a dough forms.

    Shape the dough into a disk, wrap in plastic, and refrigerate it for at least 30 minutes.

    While the dough is chilling, heat the milk, vanilla bean, and lemon zest strips in a medium saucepan until it barely starts to simmer.

    Remove the pan from the heat, cover, and steep for 10 minutes.

    Place a medium glass bowl on a damp kitchen towel or mat to prevent slipping.

    Add the egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch and whisk until thick and pale yellow.

    Remove the vanilla bean and zest strips with a slotted spoon, then discard.

    Gradually add the warm milk to the egg mixture, whisking constantly.

    Transfer the mixture back to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring frequently until it comes to a boil. Turn the heat to low and whisk constantly for 1 minute.

    In a recent development, remove the pan from the heat, then scrape the filling into a heat-proof bowl and press a piece of plastic wrap to the surface. Chill for at least 2 hours.

    In a large bowl, toss the apple slices with the lemon juice.

    Roll out the chilled dough to a 12-inch circle on a floured surface.

    Roll out the chilled dough to a 12-inch circle on a floured surface.

    Press the dough into the pan and trim the excess flush with the edge of the pan.

    Spread the cooled pastry cream evenly over the bottom of the pastry shell.

    Arrange the slices in concentric overlapping circles over the pastry cream, starting from the outer edge and working inward.

    Brush the apples with the melted butter and sprinkle on the turbinado sugar.

    Bake the crostata di mele for about 50 minutes until the crust is golden brown and the apples are tender.

    While the crostata is baking, heat the apricot jam with 1 tablespoon of water in a small saucepan until warm and liquid.

    Strain the jam if any large pieces of fruit remain.

    Remove the crostata from the oven and immediately brush on the apricot glaze.

    Cool the crostata completely in the pan on a rack before removing from the pan.

    Slice the crostata and serve at room temperature or chilled.

    Our bakery-worthy crostata di Mele (Italian apple pie) is filled with a lemon and vanilla-scented creme patissiere and topped with tart, crisp apples.

    Recent findings suggest that the crostata is one of the most continuously made dessert forms found in Italian baking, dating back to the 1400s. Not only is the crostata found in pastry shops and on restaurant menus, but it is also the one dessert that many people make at home with whatever ingredients are on hand. This kind of humble tart was likely consumed at breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

    It has been revealed that the crostata di mele probably originated in northern Italy, where apples are grown in abundance. In order to highlight the fresh flavor of the apples, crostata de mele is spiced with a light hand. Subtle cinnamon and a hint of nutmeg might be used, along with the zest of a lemon, as in this recipe. With only a few simple ingredients, the recipe is also dependent on using a light hand in preparation. The dough should be minimally handled to prevent a tough or shrunken crust. The pastry cream must be carefully tempered to prevent lumps from forming. And nothing should get in the way of the apples being the star.

    Even though there may seem to be a lot of steps to this recipe, there are lots of ways to do advance prep to save time. First, your crostata dough can be mixed, shaped into a disk, wrapped, and chilled for several days in the refrigerator. You can also freeze this dough for up to 3 months. Once you are ready to roll out the dough, allow it to come to cool to room temperature before you shape it. You can also roll out and fill your tart pan, then wrap the unbaked shell and refrigerate or freeze until it is time to fill and bake.

    In a recent development, the pastry cream should only be made 1 or 2 days in advance, and this custardy filling should not be frozen unless it is layered into a dessert (too much separation will occur). Wait until just before baking to spread the pastry cream into your tart shell so that the dough will not become soggy.

    From experience, I know that this crostata di mele will stay fresh, tasty, and sliceable for almost a week under refrigeration. That said, it is crucial to always keep the crostata chilled to prevent bacterial growth in the custard layer. Typically, 3-5 days is the best range for serving this dessert.

    #137862. 6 Best American Tex-Mex Chains, According To Customer Reviews

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    6 Best American Tex-Mex Chains, According To Customer Reviews

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1522 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that tex-Mex food is incredibly popular across the country, but the line between it and more traditional Mexican fare can be a bit hard to define.
    • Recent findings suggest that derived from Mexican and Tejano cooking methods, Tex-Mex was born out of a meeting of cultures that combined time-honored techniques and fresh ingredients.
    • Flour tortillas and dairy, like cheddar and Colby jack cheeses, are also big parts of the Tex-Mex food culture, as are queso dips and customizable combinations of rice, beans, proteins, and cheeses in a personal-sized bowl.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that tex-Mex food is incredibly popular across the country, but the line between it and more traditional Mexican fare can be a bit hard to define. Plus, there are other offshoots, like California or New Mexican styles that overlap with Tex-Mex but use different ingredients, such as avocados or hatch chiles. To cut down on some of the confusion, we've created this list to help you find the most reliable, tasty, and distinctly Tex-Mex quick service and casual restaurant chains you can dine at, according to the people who eat at them.

    Recent findings suggest that derived from Mexican and Tejano cooking methods, Tex-Mex was born out of a meeting of cultures that combined time-honored techniques and fresh ingredients. For instance, cumin and dried chili powder had recently become available, and they quickly caught on in Tex-Mex cooking. Now the pungent, earthy spices are heavily relied on for chili and stews.

    Flour tortillas and dairy, like cheddar and Colby jack cheeses, are also big parts of the Tex-Mex food culture, as are queso dips and customizable combinations of rice, beans, proteins, and cheeses in a personal-sized bowl. Or you could just put all those elements together in an oversized burrito. Many of the restaurants on this list do just that, and all of them have been highly rated by fans for taste, price, and overall value. So, the next time you're craving fajitas, quesadillas, and refried beans, feel free to give one of these chains a visit to fulfill that hunger.

    Founded in 1991, Mi Cocina is a beloved local chain with just over 20 locations throughout Texas, but the eatery's reputation stretches far further. The upscale Tex-Mex restaurant is just as known for its cocktails, especially the swirled Mambo Taxi Margarita, as it is for the food, such as the fajitas. The upscale brand's dishes include nachos al carbon, poblano chicken enchiladas, and pork picoso tamales that are so flavorful, you definitely won't want to put ketchup on them.

    Customers rate the restaurant highly on user review platforms, with diners on Yelp saying things like, "Always consistently excellent! My go-to is the brisket tacos and a Dilemma Margarita!" Other guests agree, saying they always enjoy the food when they visit the chain. That reliability is one reason people are so quick to recommend the establishment. Even those who are quite particular about their Tex-Mex fall in love with the place, and many say they'll be back after their first time dining here.

    Industry observers note that don't make the mistake of confusing Taco Cabana with Taco Bell. Both chains sell tacos, but the smaller restaurant still has a homemade feel, unlike the larger, Tex-Mex fast food super-seller. That's probably because Taco Cabana still makes its from-scratch food from fresh ingredients every day. The differences in flavor and feel in the restaurant's dishes are easy to identify, especially in the handmade flour tortillas. That helps ensure you'll never have to worry about one of the most important elements of a satisfying burrito. And the ones here come overstuffed and covered in optional cheese sauce.

    Diners here develop a passion for the chain, or as one TikTok commenter declared, "Taco Cabana is my FAVORITE fast food place. It beats Taco Bell hands down." It's not hard to see why someone might feel that way. Fans enjoy the restaurant's large portions, noting that nachos come in a box large enough to be mistaken for a pizza.

    The meats get their share of the limelight too, with customers recommending items like the beef and chicken fajita nachos, and the customizable protein bowl. One of the brand's latest hit items is the bean and cheese pie, a handheld psuedo-empanada filled with refried beans and yellow cheeses.

    Uncle Julio's is an eatery that has understood the importance of making every dish from scratch since it opened several decades ago, and that includes the flour tortillas. The freshly made flatbread definitely tastes better than store-bought ones, which is why people can buy them by the dozen. And that's just one of the things that's made with care here. Dishes like guacamole that's made tableside and large burritos have led this Texas-based chain to expand into more than 30 locations.

    People appreciate the restaurant's salsa, which holds a great middle-ground between mild and spicy, and praise the bacon-wrapped shrimp, which pairs juicy, seasoned seafood with crispy and chewy slices of pork. Others say they often have enough of their meal left to take some home, especially with dishes like the chicken and steak fajitas or the Tex-Mex combination dinner.

    Sources indicate that this Tex-Mex establishment also has a unique dessert – interactive chocolate piñatas. Guests are encouraged to play with their food when the hanging ball of decorated chocolate is brought to the table. A few short taps later and the dessert cracks open to spill strawberries, churros, and other fruits onto the tray. It's another delicious and memorable way Uncle Julio's has found to fuse cultures before ending the evening.

    Recent findings suggest that like several of the chains on this list, Fuzzy's Taco Shop was founded in Texas. But this one has gone on to become one of the largest of the homegrown brands, with more than 100 locations in 14 states. That growth was spurred forward by customers who enjoy the restaurant's sizable portions, flavors, and consistency on dishes ranging from breakfast burritos, quesadillas, nachos, and customizable bowls.

    First-time diners are impressed by the guacamole and overall experience of eating at Fuzzy's, and say they'll no doubt be returning soon. Others make it a point to visit the chain often, saying it's a great spot for birria tacos. In fact, one fan on Facebook called the dish "top notch," adding that the meal was perfectly made. Items like the grilled steak bowl and seasoned chips are so tasty they can even help people who normally eat at other Mexican-inspired places make the switch to Fuzzy's.

    Guests are warmly greeted every time they walk through the doors at Moe's Southwest Grill, a tradition the business started at the first location in 2000. Since then, the manufacturer has grown rapidly, now operating almost 550 stores across the nation. The brand is known for innovative flavors and good quality, and customers praise the queso, overstuffed burritos, and customizable bowls, which many say are better than other national brands.

    A TikTok user posted about their experience getting a nearly full bag of chips after ordering his mains, and that kind of generosity isn't rare at the chain. Another fan noted how stuffed the birria stack they ordered was, saying it was heavy to pick up, while a first-time diner was impressed by how large the bowl they ordered was.

    According to recent reports, fans of Moe's have plenty of choices to customize their bowls and other meals with, but many find their favorite items and stick with them. That loyalty had one customer declaring a half-hour drive to the nearest store wasn't too far to go for the food, showing that not even a little distance can keep people away when a queso craving strikes. Or, as one Tripadvisor reviewer said, "... food is splendid! All around just great establishment. We loved everything, especially the queso!!".

    The name Qdoba Mexican Eats might catch your attention, but it's the chain's food that keeps it. So much so that in the almost 30 years the restaurant has been open, Qdoba fans have formed a rivalry with those who prefer Chipotle, which just so happens to have also been founded in Denver in the 1990s. But Colorado residents prefer the smaller chain, with customers citing the brand's freshness, taste, and generosity with the queso keeps other national brands from comparing.

    Industry observers note that the establishment is known for the variety of fillings it offers, including steak and chicken that's grilled in-house. In addition to burrito bowls, you can customize a bowl of layered nachos, too. And the quesadillas can have some crunch added with a cheesy exterior crust. One Facebook user was so impressed by the restaurant that they posted, "I've been 5 times, the food is always fresh and hot [...] I've tried their quesadillas and bowl and I'm absolutely blown away every time with the quality. 10/10!".

    According to recent reports, tex-Mex chains are popular and plentiful on the restaurant landscape, so narrowing down this list to the brands fans can't stop raving about took a bit of time. First, the criteria for how we'd be defining what makes a chain the best and what made it Tex-Mex were decided.

    If the restaurants had a focus on flour tortillas, yellow cheeses, and cumin, alongside dishes, like nachos, enchiladas, fajitas, and queso, it qualified as a Tex-Mex establishment.

    Industry observers note that the eateries had to have more than a dozen locations and good reviews for taste, value, and consistency across multiple sources. Those platforms included social media posts and comments, message boards, user review sites, and professional reviews. The final list was compiled after each chain's specific instances of customer satisfaction were tallied.

    #137858. Add This Ingredient To French Toast For A Crispier Crust (Hint: It's Not Butter Or Oil)

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (614 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Add This Ingredient To French Toast For A Crispier Crust (Hint: It's Not Butter Or Oil)

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (614 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that A classic French toast recipe is one of those comforting dishes that can be whipped up in a matter of minutes.
    • Recent findings suggest that semolina is a coarse, pale-yellow flour made by grinding the endosperm of durum wheat, one of the hardest species of wheat there is.
    • Semolina is still flour, so balance is key.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that A classic French toast recipe is one of those comforting dishes that can be whipped up in a matter of minutes. However, one common problem people run into is soggy bread rather than a crisp, beautifully caramelized exterior. Unfortunately, sogginess is something of an occupational hazard when you're soaking bread in liquid. To give your slices more of a chance to thrive, all you need to do is add a little semolina flour to your soaking mixture. Two tablespoons per cup and a half of liquid is just about all you need.

    Recent findings suggest that semolina is a coarse, pale-yellow flour made by grinding the endosperm of durum wheat, one of the hardest species of wheat there is. Compared to standard, powdery all-purpose flour, semolina is higher in protein and fiber, and its coarse grains are well-suited to soaking up moisture. In French toast, that can be the difference between a soggy exterior and a crispy one. A small amount turns a watery custard into a more structured batter that clings to the bread instead of letting it drink up all that liquid and fall apart before it even reaches the frying pan. Its subtle nuttiness also adds a whole new layer of complexity to the flavor of the French toast, and would pair wonderfully with some cosy nutmeg and cinnamon.

    Just don't go overboard. Semolina is still flour, so balance is key. Add too little and the mixture stays watery; add too much, and you end up with something closer to a paste than a batter. We recommend starting with a small amount, around a tablespoon, then adjusting until you reach your desired consistency. Semolina flour takes time to absorb liquid, so once you've added it, let the custard sit for a minimum of 10 minutes before adding your bread. Once it's rested, it should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

    Semolina is one way to give French toast a crispy, lightly browned exterior, but it's by no means the only one. If you're having a hard time finding it, you can always swap in regular flour. The texture is different, but flour also absorbs liquid and thickens the batter, so you get largely the same effect, just without the nutty flavor. You could even skip the flour altogether and stir a cornstarch slurry into the custard, which packs even more thickening power. Just remember, as with semolina, moderation is key when adding flour or cornstarch into the mix.

    Beyond thickening the custard, there are plenty of other handy tricks for shatteringly crispy French toast. To improve both its texture and flavor, give your bread a generous dusting of sugar after it comes out of the custard (before it hits the heat). Alton Brown might prefer honey over sugar in his French toast, but we'd argue that's a rare mistake. See, once sugar hits the heat, it starts to caramelize, melting into a crisp, brûléed crust and infusing the bread with a rich, toasty flavor. Keep the heat moderate, since caramelization can rapidly turn to burning without proper care.

    If you're not sold on the idea of messing around with the batter or adding extra ingredients, you can guarantee crispy French toast from the get-go by using stale bread. This might not sound too appetizing, but hear us out. Bread that's around one to two days old has lost a good chunk of its moisture, which leaves it firmer and drier. It acts like a sponge, soaking up the custard without turning to mush, so you get a rich, eggy center and a browned exterior instead of a soggy, limp slice.

    Sources indicate that women who changed their usual lunchtime drink lost 41 per cent more weight over 18 months. What made the difference?

    Women who changed their usual lunchtime drink lost 41 per cent more weight over 18 months. What made the difference?

    Swapping diet drinks for water could help people lose more weight.

    Women with type 2 diabetes who make the switch lose around 41 percent more weight over 18 months than those who continue drinking diet beverages.

    They are also twice as likely to achieve diabetes remission during a structured weight-management programme.

    The findings raise a question about whether a drink’s calorie count tells the whole story about its effects on weight.

    Sweet taste without the accompanying energy might influence appetite signals.

    The results suggest that everyday drink choices could play a useful supporting role in longer-term weight management.

    The research involved around 80 women who were overweight or had obesity, had type 2 diabetes and regularly consumed diet drinks.

    Researchers randomly assigned them either to replace their usual diet beverage with water after lunch five times a week or to continue drinking it.

    Both groups took part in a six-month weight-loss programme followed by a year devoted to maintaining their progress.

    By the end, women assigned to water had lost an average of 6.82 kg, compared with 4.85 kg among those continuing with diet drinks.

    The difference amounted to almost 2 kg of additional weight loss across the programme.

    The water group also revealed greater improvements in measures including fasting blood glucose, insulin resistance and blood fats.

    Diabetes remission was reported in 90 percent of women assigned to water, compared with 45 percent of those continuing diet beverages.

    Industry observers note that dr Hamid R. Farshchi, study co-author, mentioned:.

    “It’s a small change with the potential for a major impact on long-term health outcomes.”.

    The brain may respond differently when a sweet taste arrives without the energy normally supplied by sugar.

    In a separate experiment involving around 75 adults, participants reported greater hunger after consuming sucralose than sugar, and the sweetener altered activity in the hypothalamus, a brain region involved in appetite regulation (Chakravartti et al., 2025).

    However, hunger ratings after sucralose did not differ from those after water, so the findings do not establish that sweetened drinks necessarily make people hungrier than plain water.

    The mismatch between sweetness and energy might help explain some appetite responses, but whether it contributed to the weight-loss difference remains unknown.

    The study was published in the journal Diabetes (Farshchi Nasr et al., 2025).

    • It has been revealed that chili is one of those meals that scratches an itch that no other comfort food can quite compare to.
    • Instant coffee crystals will add some bold, roasted richness to your chili.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    It has been revealed that chili is one of those meals that scratches an itch that no other comfort food can quite compare to. You can go with beans or no beans, or even make a super satisfying vegan version. A big batch can be pretty easy to make in the slow cooker, but despite the simple prep, it still takes a lot of time. So, when you want a quick hit, you can always reach for your favorite brand of the canned stuff. However, there's an easy trick to up the flavor of your meal — add a dash of instant coffee. The incredible blend of flavors might just blow your mind.

    Instant coffee crystals will add some bold, roasted richness to your chili. Sure, coffee is bitter, but if you don't go overboard, its presence will be subtle, making your chili taste more like something homemade that's been simmering on the stove all day. It creates a nice depth by enhancing the perception of the beefy umami and highlighting spices like cumin, coriander, cayenne, and chili powder. It can also help offset some of the perceived acidity in the tomato-heavy sauce, giving you an end result that's more balanced on the palate and beautifully tied together.

    If you don't already have instant coffee in the pantry, instant espresso, like Medaglia D'Oro Instant Espresso, is sometimes preferred because it dissolves more easily, but really, any instant coffee will work. Just keep in mind that espresso will have a stronger flavor, and the strength of any given coffee crystals can vary a bit. Start with just a pinch, or about a ¼ teaspoon per 15-ounce can of chili. You can dissolve it in a few spoonfuls of hot water first to ensure it doesn't clump, but if the chili is already simmering, it should blend in easily, especially in small amounts. Give it a taste and add more if you'd like.

    In a recent development, if you want to go for bolder undertones, a touch of cocoa powder pairs nicely with coffee crystals. If you want to skip the instant coffee and use the real thing, you can add a little brewed coffee or finely ground espresso (but when using the latter, you'll need to mix it into a paste with some water so you don't end up with a mouthful of grounds). A splash of bourbon, or even beer, can help round out the flavor with the coffee. And much like it works in chili, instant coffee can wake up your spaghetti sauce. But to get that great earthy, bold flavor in a full meal right off the shelf, you're going to want to try coffee crystals in your canned chili.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that at first glance, tuna salad may appear to be a fairly set-in-stone formula. You mix the tinned fish with mayo, add in some aromatics, and enjoy the dish on bread or standalone. Yet start trialing creative add-ins, and tuna salad welcomes a surprisingly wide array of ingredients. There are so many ways to take plain tuna salad to the next level. A sharp cheddar cheese is one unexpected flavor boost.

    After all, creaminess is a central part of the dish's appeal. And as a dairy product, cheddar cheese offers such a smooth mouthfeel in spades. However, unlike a simple mayo dressing, the cheese comes with a punch. Aging develops complex flavors, which can vary from barely perceptible tartness to rich nuttiness to a bold bite. Usually, the older the cheddar, the more amplified the flavor — although as the cheese develops, it loses some creaminess to become crumbly.

    According to recent reports, for a top-tier cheddar tuna salad, go with a balanced option, aged for around six to nine months. Usually classified specifically as sharp, such a cheese is right when the acidic flavors turn into a bold bite — perfect for a tuna salad. So cube up the cheese, using two ounces per can of tuna, then stir everything up with some salt, onions, celery, and your other go-to tuna salad fold-ins. You'll get a dish that's still comforting, but also comes with revamped flair.

    As America's favorite cheese, cheddar certainly belongs in a dish like tuna salad. While it's not common to mix cheese directly into the salad, the inclusion is reminiscent of a beloved tuna salad application: a tuna melt. Originating by mistake, the tuna melt proves that fish and cheese do belong on the same plate, especially if tuna's involved.

    Further embrace the two dishes by heating the cheddar cheese tuna salad. The cheese will turn molten inside — not only on top — of the fish, making for an extra-satisfying filling. Pair that with a nice bread, say a classic American white loaf, a deli-inspired rye, or a dependable sourdough, and you've got a terrific sandwich on your hands.

    Sources indicate that not to say there's not more magic to explore with a cold cheddar tuna salad, too. The cheesy rendition is a befitting tuna pasta salad twist. Or balance out cheddar's richness by rolling the salad into lettuce wraps, a delicious appetizer option. Cheddar gives tuna salad that extra oomph, turning the basic dish into a centerpiece meal.
